segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, thanks for making time, Dana. I pulled up the quote we discussed: 42 user seats, the implementation package, and the standard support plan. Total comes to $38,760 for a 12-month term starting June 1.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Yep, that matches what I had. The only thing I need to confirm is whether those 42 seats can be split across our operations and finance teams, or if they all need to sit under one admin.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: They can be split. You’ll have one primary admin, but we can set up department groups for operations and finance during onboarding. No extra cost for that.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay, good. And for invoicing, can you do annual upfront, but send the invoice after May 20? Our current budget cycle closes that week.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, that’s fine. I’ll note invoice to be issued May 21, net 30. So payment due June 20. Does that work with procurement?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: It should. They may ask for the order form by this Friday, though, because legal only meets on Tuesdays.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Got it. I can get the order form out today. The terms are our standard 12-month agreement, auto-renewal with 60 days’ notice, and the data processing addendum attached.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: On auto-renewal, can we make the notice period 45 days? That’s what our template usually allows.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, that’s a reasonable redline. I’ll send that through deal desk, but I don’t expect an issue. It may take a day to turn.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Perfect. Last thing, we’re targeting a July 8 go-live. Is that still realistic if we sign by May 31?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes. With signature by May 31, kickoff the week of June 3, configuration and data import in June, July 8 is realistic. I’ll include that project timeline in the email.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Send it over to me and copy Marcus from procurement. I’ll route it internally once it lands.
